correctness.rationale: The model uses uniform recurrent states of each graph separately; stationary grain addition is a recurrent-group permutation, so E T=L^{-1}e_1 and total E M=1^TL^{-1}e_1. On C_n with sink 0, the Dirichlet path Green G_ab=min(a,b)(n-max(a,b))/n solves the difference equations with zero boundary; u_a=a(n-a)/2, so M(C_n)=(n-1)/2. A nonsink chord changes L to L+bb^T, b=e_i-e_j; Sherman–Morrison gives ΔM= -(L^{-1}b)_1 (b^Tu)/(1+b^TL^{-1}b). Verified (L^{-1}b)_1=d/n, b^Tu=-d(n-i-j)/2, and b^TL^{-1}b=d(n-d)/n, proving exactly ΔM=d²(n-i-j)/(2[n+d(n-d)]). All denominators positive and d≥2. The n=4 only chord {1,3} is neutral; n=5 {1,3} gives +2/11. For incident chord k=1+d, 2≤d≤n-3, 0<d²(n-d-2)/((n-1)(n+d(n-d)))<1 (both factors strictly smaller than their denominator bounds), proving 1<Mnew/Mold<2; taking k=n-floor(sqrt n) yields d/n→1 and (n-d)/sqrt n→1 so ratio→2. Independently written exact rational grounded-Laplacian solver tested every 165 valid chord through n=12, and independent burning/recurrent-state stabilizations for all 20 chords through n=7 reproduced the exact means and counts. Four n up to 10^6 show ratio convergence, not an infinite proof. Original repository checker was separately source-inspected; its claimed 120/20 cases are consistent with independent checks. This is an exact first-moment proof, not avalanche area/distribution stochastic dominance.
residual_risks: All-n proof invokes standard finite recurrent group permutation and invertibility; independent finite tests alone cannot prove it.
No claim is established for sink-touching chords, other grain injection positions, nonrecurrent input, total distinct affected vertices or stochastic domination.
Factor-two limit applies only to source-incident chord family; no global amplification bound for other graph families.

value.rationale: A structurally natural dynamical observable (stationary total toppling work after a fixed source addition) responds unexpectedly to an added edge. The exact two-endpoint criterion i+j<n,=n,>n partitions all permissible nonsink chords into increased, neutral and decreased mean and identifies the sharp threshold using actual graph positions, not an arbitrary computational slice. The smallest strict example at n=5 and an incident-chord family with finite ratio below two but asymptotic limit two reveal a motivated sharp magnitude boundary. This nontrivial infinite family classification may be used to check intuitions about avalanche activity and link augmentation despite relying on familiar linear-algebra tools. It neither claims novelty for Sherman–Morrison nor general stochastic dominance.
residual_risks: The proof is short because of standard Green rank-one identities, so its independent mathematical value rests on a useful sign-complete and sharp factor-two interpretation rather than new techniques.
Only expected total topplings are covered; extensions to arbitrary graphs and distributional ordering are open in this package.

final_claim: For n≥4, sink 0 and addition at 1 in uniformly recurrent Abelian sandpiles, inserting any previously absent nonsink chord {i,j} (1≤i<j≤n−1,j−i≥2) changes expected total individual topplings by (j−i)^2(n−i−j)/(2[n+(j−i)(n−j+i)]). Thus the sign is exactly the sign of n−i−j; source-incident chords can approach but never attain a factor-two amplification within the stated family.
limitations: Exact stationary mean on fixed sink/injection and nonsink simple chords only, no full distribution or random-source theorem.
Best-of-knowledge originality, historical noncoverage not certified; short standard-matrix derivability is explicit.
Underlying same-model review and VERIFY_OK are not substitutes for the independent C/O/V reasoning.
Finite enumeration verifies finite cases only; all-n follows from proved algebra.
